pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.summary: How Fayegram's plugins and marketplace website handle user-directed content, local files, and third-party services.

sections.heading: Scope
paragraphs: This policy applies to Faye Codex Utility, Faye Coding Assistant, Faye Image Utility, Faye UI System Engineer, and the Faye Plugin Market website. Fayegram is the team publishing and maintaining these plugins. The plugins run inside the user's host environment and do not operate a Fayegram account service or backend.

sections.heading: What Fayegram collects
paragraphs: Fayegram does not receive or retain plugin prompts, repository content, images, browser conversations, generated files, or usage telemetry on an independently operated server. The reviewed plugin packages contain no Fayegram analytics, advertising, tracking, account system, or independent network client.

The marketplace website is a static catalog. It has no sign-in, contact form, advertising, or Fayegram analytics. Its hosting provider may process ordinary request data such as IP address, device or browser information, requested URL, and timestamps to deliver and secure the site under the provider's own terms.

sections.heading: Data the plugins may handle
paragraphs: Depending on the workflow the user chooses, a plugin may handle the following data in the user's host environment for the purpose of completing that request:
items: Prompts, instructions, task context, and limited conversation excerpts.
Repository files, paths, source text, file sizes, line counts, Git state, test output, and other workspace evidence used for coding or source-file token estimation.

Images, image paths, base64 image data, visible image content, prompts associated with images, and deterministic image measurements used for conversion, editing, artifact review, or user-requested age-rating estimates.

When the user explicitly requests an image age-rating estimate, the visible image content may include mature or potentially sensitive subjects such as violence, blood or gore, nudity, sexual content, substances, horror, or strong language. The utility analyzes only what is visibly needed for the requested estimate and does not identify people or infer sensitive personal traits.
Local saved-prompt notes, browser screenshots, compact session notes, reports, and generated image files when the user requests or authorizes those outputs.
Supported ChatGPT/Gemini chat identity, limited conversation content, conversation URLs, and user-directed messages; when Browser Use is selected, relevant page and composer state.

sections.heading: Recipients and external transmission
paragraphs: The selected host and its model or subagent services process information under the user's account, workspace, and applicable provider terms. For Codex, these are the relevant OpenAI services and terms. Fayegram does not receive a separate copy merely because a Fayegram plugin was used.

The LLM Chat Operator uses a complete purpose-built ChatGPT capability when it covers the request, or supported ChatGPT/Gemini browser pages when Browser Use is selected or required. User-directed messages and explicitly authorized content are transmitted to the selected service, operated by OpenAI or Google. Fayegram is not an intermediary for that transmission, does not receive the content, and does not control the service's collection, use, retention, model-training choices, or account settings.

Other reviewed plugin scripts process files locally and do not independently call Fayegram or third-party network services. Users should not provide credentials, authentication secrets, payment-card data, government identifiers, protected health information, or other restricted data to a plugin.

sections.heading: Storage and retention
paragraphs: Fayegram does not set a retention period for plugin content because Fayegram does not receive or store that content. Local notes, screenshots, reports, converted images, and edited images remain where the user or plugin placed them until the user deletes them. Repository history or backups may preserve copies according to the user's own tools and settings.

Host, model-provider, browser, workspace, and hosting-provider retention is controlled by those services and the user's account or organization settings. Users should review and use the deletion, temporary-chat, history, and privacy controls offered by the applicable service.

sections.heading: User choices and controls
items: Choose what prompts, files, images, paths, and context to provide.
Do not invoke a workflow that is not appropriate for the content involved.
Review proposed browser or file-changing actions and withhold authorization when needed.
Delete local plugin outputs using normal filesystem and repository tools.
Use the account, chat-history, temporary-chat, privacy, and deletion controls provided by the applicable host or service for content sent to it.

sections.heading: Changes and questions
paragraphs: Fayegram may update this policy when the plugins, website, or applicable publication requirements change. The effective date above identifies this policy version when published. Fayegram does not offer individual privacy or technical-support correspondence for these plugins.

sections.heading: Acceptance and scope
paragraphs: These Terms are provided by the Fayegram team and apply to Faye Codex Utility, Faye Coding Assistant, Faye Image Utility, Faye UI System Engineer, and the Faye Plugin Market website. By installing, accessing, or using them, the user agrees to these Terms. If the user does not agree, the user should not use them.
These Terms supplement, and do not replace, the terms that apply to the selected host, its provider, the user's browser or workspace, and any other service the user chooses to use.

sections.heading: Permitted use
paragraphs: Any software license included in a distributed plugin package controls the rights it grants for that package. These Terms do not narrow, replace, or add restrictions to those package-license rights. Separately identified Fayegram identity assets remain subject to the identity-asset policy included with the applicable package.
items: Use the plugins only for lawful purposes and within the permissions granted by the user and the host environment.
Do not use the plugins to bypass access controls, service restrictions, rate limits, safety measures, or third-party terms.
Do not provide credentials, authentication secrets, payment-card data, government identifiers, protected health information, or other restricted data to the plugins.

sections.heading: User responsibility
paragraphs: The user controls the inputs, requested actions, accounts, local files, and third-party services used with the plugins. The user is responsible for reviewing actions and outputs, maintaining backups, obtaining necessary rights and permissions, and deciding whether a result is suitable for its intended use. Neither these Terms nor a package license claims or changes ownership of user inputs or outputs.

Coding recommendations, web UI audit findings, generated or edited images, artifact findings, and token estimates may be incomplete or inaccurate. Image age-rating results are informational still-image analogies only; they are not official ratings, certifications, legal advice, moderation decisions, or viewer-age verification.

sections.heading: Third-party services
paragraphs: The LLM Chat Operator can send user-directed content through a supported direct ChatGPT capability or supported ChatGPT/Gemini browser sessions. Those services are operated by OpenAI and Google, not Fayegram. The user is responsible for the account used, the content sent, and compliance with the applicable service terms. Fayegram does not control third-party availability, security, data practices, outputs, account actions, or changes to those services.

A direction from the user to use a third-party service does not authorize the plugin to evade that service's rules. Fayegram's disclaimers do not replace any authorization or compliance required by a third-party service or distribution platform.

To the fullest extent permitted by law, Fayegram disclaims express and implied warranties, including merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement.

The Fayegram team does not provide individual technical support, guaranteed maintenance, response times, service-level commitments, or a commitment to add features or fix a particular issue. Self-service information may be changed or withdrawn at any time.

sections.heading: Changes and discontinuation

sections.heading: No support channel
paragraphs: Fayegram does not provide an individual support channel for these plugins. Fayegram plugins are provided as is, without a help desk, ticket system, guaranteed response time, service-level agreement, compatibility commitment, or maintenance obligation.

sections.heading: Self-service steps
items: Confirm that your host is current and that the intended plugin is available and enabled through that host’s supported setup.
Open the plugin's catalog entry and read the included skill instructions, boundaries, dependencies, and expected invocation wording.
Use an explicit skill invocation when the skill requires one, and provide only the files and context needed for the task.
Review the host error, plugin output, local permissions, dependency versions, and the current workspace state before retrying.
If a host feature or third-party website changed, use that provider's own documentation and support resources.

sections.heading: Third-party and host issues

Account, billing, outage, data-retention, abuse, and platform-access questions must be handled through the applicable provider's controls and support process. Do not send passwords, API keys, one-time codes, session cookies, or other secrets while seeking help.

methods.summary: Install selected plugin folders from a local copy of the marketplace.

verification.scope: Local installation and one representative skill were checked on the recorded version. This does not certify every workflow, operating system, or app interface.

agentRules: Identify the selected product, interface, Git or local method, operating system/shell, and desired plugins. Ask only for missing decisions; reuse the user's existing authorization.

Read this target's setup.json, manifest.json, and native registry. Use their actual marketplace identity, repository URL, available plugin IDs, versions, and skills. Do not borrow facts from another target.

A route marked needs-input is not executable guidance. Describe the missing procedure and ask for the user's demonstration or confirmation. Never guess app controls or treat a placeholder as evidence.
Inspect existing registrations and installed packages using supported read-only commands. Reuse a matching source and installed version. Explain conflicts before replacing anything.

Choose the declared shell variant. Run only the selected route and plugins, using automation output flags where provided. Interactive slash commands belong in the product, not the operating-system shell.
Keep authentication in the application's supported sign-in flow. Never ask for credentials in a prompt. Respect existing trust authorization; do not silently add automatic trust flags.
Preserve unrelated settings and working installations. Do not clear caches, remove unrelated packages, rewrite global configuration wholesale, or weaken permissions to make setup pass.
Verify installed identity, version, enabled state where exposed, and skill discovery. A zero exit code or copied files alone do not establish successful setup.
Start or request a fresh session when needed. Run a functional skill request only if the user authorizes that execution; installation does not require a model call.
Report the selected route, packages installed or reused, observed verification, and the next user action. Separate documented behavior, observations, and untested or blocked work.

troubleshooting.title: The terminal does not recognize the command
troubleshooting.reason: The application may be missing, unavailable in this terminal, or too old for plugin commands.
steps: Open a new terminal after installing the application.
Check its version and plugin help against the official command reference.
Do not paste interactive slash commands into the system terminal.
troubleshooting.expected: The application starts and its plugin commands or Plugins interface are available.

troubleshooting.title: The Git repository cannot be added
troubleshooting.reason: The URL, network connection, or Git access may prevent fetching the marketplace.
steps: Compare the source with the repository address in your selected guide.
Confirm access through your normal Git authentication flow; private repositories require access.
Retry after resolving access. Do not disable certificate checks or paste a token into the guide.
troubleshooting.expected: The intended marketplace is listed without an access error.

troubleshooting.title: The local folder is not recognized
troubleshooting.reason: Marketplace registration uses the repository root; direct plugin installation uses an individual plugin folder.
steps: For Codex or Grok registration, open the directory containing the marketplace registry and plugins folder.
For Antigravity terminal installation, select plugins/<plugin-id> inside that checkout.
Keep the existing checkout; do not delete it to retry registration.
troubleshooting.expected: The source is recognized and the desired packages are available.

troubleshooting.title: The plugin is installed but its skills are missing
troubleshooting.reason: The session may predate installation, the plugin may be disabled, or a skill may require explicit invocation.
steps: Check the plugin's installed and enabled state.
Start a fresh session and open the skill picker or the selected plugin's skill guide.
Check invocation and tool requirements. Installation does not grant extra tools or permissions.
troubleshooting.expected: Applicable skills can be discovered or explicitly invoked in the new session.

troubleshooting.title: Grok does not show a newly installed skill
troubleshooting.reason: Discovery output can distinguish an unloaded package from a skill requiring an explicit request.
steps: Check the plugin is enabled in /plugins, then start a new session.
Run the optional discovery command below and look for the selected plugin and its expected skill names.
If the package is present but a skill is not offered automatically, read its invocation requirements.
troubleshooting.expected: The applicable skill names appear, or an explicit-invocation requirement explains the difference.

troubleshooting.title: The same plugin is already installed
troubleshooting.reason: A matching installation can be reused; another source may create ambiguity.
steps: Compare the installed identity, source, and version with this guide.
For another version or source, follow the product's update procedure after deciding which source to keep.
troubleshooting.expected: The intended source and version are identified without removing unrelated registrations.

codex.label: Codex
codex.evidence: Explicit dollar-prefixed skill invocations in the packaged skill instructions and maintained examples. This is documentation evidence, not a new native-host installation test.

grok.label: Grok
grok.evidence: Grok Build documents user-invocable skills as slash commands: https://docs.x.ai/build/features/skills-plugins-marketplaces (checked 2026-09-27). This documents invocation syntax, not support for every skill's tools or workflow.

antigravity.evidence: Antigravity documents CLI skill-to-slash-command conversion: https://www.antigravity.google/docs/skills/#slash-command-conversion (checked 2026-09-27). This documents invocation syntax, not support for every skill's tools or workflow.
